claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately represents paragraph (a) general prohibition on takeoff with inoperative instruments or equipment unless the conditions are met or paragraph (d) applies.
Claim C0001 correctly captures the requirement under paragraph (a)(1) that an approved Minimum Equipment List must exist for the aircraft.

Claim C0002 correctly captures the requirement under paragraph (a)(2) that the aircraft have within it a letter of authorization issued by the responsible Flight Standards office authorizing operation under the MEL.
Claim C0003 correctly reflects the provision in paragraph (a)(2) stating that the letter of authorization may be obtained by written request of the airworthiness certificate holder.
Claim C0004 accurately conveys the statement in paragraph (a)(2) that the MEL and letter of authorization constitute a supplemental type certificate for the aircraft.

Claim C0005 completely captures both required elements of paragraph (a)(3): preparation in accordance with paragraph (b) limitations and provision for operation with instruments/equipment in an inoperable condition.
Claim C0006 accurately represents paragraph (a)(4) regarding the entry describing inoperable instruments and equipment in aircraft records available to the pilot.
Claim C0007 correctly states the condition in paragraph (a)(5) requiring operation under all applicable conditions and limitations in the MEL and letter of authorization.
Claim C0008 fully specifies the three categories of instruments and equipment that may not be included in a Minimum Equipment List pursuant to paragraph (b).
Claim C0009 correctly conveys paragraph (c) requirement that authorized persons under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 must use the approved MEL to comply with § 91.213.
Claim C0010 accurately and comprehensively captures the permission and all four conditions of paragraph (d) for takeoff without an approved MEL.

Claim C0011 correctly specifies the rule in paragraph (d)(3)(ii) that if deactivation of the inoperative instrument or equipment involves maintenance, it must be accomplished and recorded in accordance with part 43.
Claim C0012 accurately conveys the closing provision of paragraph (d) regarding properly altered condition acceptable to the Administrator.
Claim C0013 correctly reflects paragraph (e) permission allowing operation with inoperable instruments or equipment under a special flight permit pursuant to §§ 21.197 and 21.199.

unit_judgments.rationale: The prohibition and scope of paragraph (a) are fully retained by claim C0000.
The requirement in paragraph (a)(1) that an approved MEL exists for the aircraft is fully retained by claim C0001.
The requirement in paragraph (a)(2) regarding the letter of authorization being within the aircraft is fully covered by claim C0002.
The permission in paragraph (a)(2) to obtain the letter of authorization by written request of the airworthiness certificate holder is fully covered by claim C0003.
The legal effect stated in paragraph (a)(2) that the MEL and letter constitute a supplemental type certificate is covered by claim C0004.
The requirement in paragraph (a)(3)(i) that the MEL be prepared in accordance with paragraph (b) limitations is fully covered by claim C0005.
The requirement in paragraph (a)(3)(ii) that the MEL provide for operation in an inoperable condition is fully covered by claim C0005.
The requirement in paragraph (a)(4) for aircraft records available to the pilot to include an entry describing inoperable equipment is covered by claim C0006.
The requirement in paragraph (a)(5) that the aircraft be operated under all applicable MEL and letter conditions and limitations is covered by claim C0007.
The prohibition in paragraph (b)(1) against including airworthiness-required essential equipment in the MEL is covered by claim C0008.
The prohibition in paragraph (b)(2) regarding AD-required equipment in the MEL is covered by claim C0008.
The prohibition in paragraph (b)(3) regarding equipment required for specific operations by Part 91 is covered by claim C0008.
The mandate in paragraph (c) requiring authorized persons under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use that MEL is covered by claim C0009.
The paragraph (d)(1)(i) category for operation without an MEL is completely preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d)(1)(ii) category for operation without an MEL is completely preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d)(2)(i) condition excluding VFR-day type certification equipment is completely preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d)(2)(ii) condition excluding equipment indicated as required on equipment lists is preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d)(2)(iii) condition excluding equipment required by § 91.205 or other Part 91 rules is preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d)(2)(iv) condition excluding equipment required by an AD is preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d)(3)(i) alternative for removal, placarding, and maintenance recording is preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d)(3)(ii) alternative for deactivation and placarding, along with maintenance compliance under Part 43, is covered jointly by claims C0010 and C0011.
The paragraph (d)(4) hazard determination requirement by an authorized pilot or maintenance person is preserved within claim C0010.
The paragraph (d) concluding statement regarding properly altered condition acceptable to the Administrator is covered by claim C0012.
The paragraph (e) provision authorizing operation under a special flight permit is covered by claim C0013.
